traps.title: renamed clamp copy
traps.trick: identical body, all names changed

traps.title: sum is not clamp
traps.trick: different algorithm, same domain

traps.title: inlined helpers money formatter
traps.trick: Canon delegates to two small helpers; the app inlines their bodies and swaps template literals for concatenation. Same logic, different call graph.

traps.title: parameterized pagination copy
traps.trick: Same pagination algorithm with every identifier renamed, the per-page cap literal changed 100 -> 50, and return keys renamed. Same AST shape, different names AND literals.

traps.title: linear search is not binary search
traps.trick: linearSearch shares binarySearch's exact signature, domain and index-or--1 contract, but is an O(n) scan with no halving. Tempting look-alike, different algorithm.

traps.title: reduce becomes a for loop
traps.trick: weightedAverage's reduce() with an accumulator object is rewritten as an explicit for loop with two mutable lets. Same math, very different AST — the rewrite genuinely dilutes the signal.

traps.title: early returns become nested ifs
traps.trick: Two early-return guards become nested positive ifs with a single fall-through return 0. The statement multiset is nearly unchanged while the control-flow shape is inverted.

traps.title: if/else chain becomes ternary chain
traps.trick: The if/else-if status classification collapses into a nested ternary chain with identical range comparisons and labels. Same branches, different statement kinds.

traps.title: destructured options with defaults
traps.trick: Plain optional params defaulted inside the body become a destructured options object with default parameters. The body is identical; only the signature is reshaped.

traps.title: zip pairs is not deep merge
traps.trick: mergePairs zips parallel key/value arrays into a record; deepMerge recursively merges two records. Same combine-into-a-Record domain and out-variable plumbing, unrelated algorithms.

traps.title: async/await becomes .then chain
traps.trick: The fetch-validate-project steps of loadUser are rewritten as a .then() chain with identical messages, checks and projection. Awaits become arrows; the steps are the same.

traps.title: try/catch becomes .catch with error object
traps.trick: try/catch with thrown errors becomes Promise.resolve().then().catch() returning an {ok,value,error} object, and sync becomes async. The validation core is identical but everything around it dilutes the signal.

traps.title: shared boilerplate, different core
traps.trick: computeShipping copies computeTax's entire validation shell and return contract but replaces the short tax core with a longer zone/express/free-threshold shipping algorithm. Boilerplate twins, different cores — must NOT be duplicate.

traps.title: format is the inverse of parse
traps.trick: formatQueryString is the exact inverse of parseQueryString (record -> string instead of string -> record), sharing the encode/decode/+/&/= vocabulary but with opposite data flow.

traps.title: string clamp vs numeric snap
traps.trick: snapToGrid mirrors truncateText's clamp skeleton (guard, normalize a limit, early return when within bounds, combine a remainder) but works on numbers with modulo arithmetic and round-up/down branching instead of string length + slice.

traps.title: recursion becomes an explicit stack
traps.trick: Recursive deepFlatten is rewritten with an explicit reversed LIFO stack that preserves output order. Same algorithm and result, no recursion — heavy structural dilution.

traps.title: named helpers reorder the pipeline
traps.trick: The same paid-orders revenue pipeline: inline arrows become named intermediate helpers, map/filter order is swapped (the map only projects, so semantics are preserved), and the reduce accumulator flattens to a number.

traps.title: reordered consts and spread assembly
traps.trick: Same profile object: the independent consts are reordered, the result is assembled via a spread of a partial base plus remaining keys, and property order is shuffled. Identical computations, different plumbing.

traps.title: one canon function split in two
traps.trick: processRecord is split into cleanRecord (validate + clamp) and formatGrade (grade + render); their combined bodies equal the canon body except the error seam returns null. Expect similar via parts — cleanRecord is the larger half.

traps.title: mirror-image loop
traps.trick: isSortedAscending's forward prev > curr scan becomes a backward curr < prev scan with an inverted length guard and swapped pairwise locals. Same algorithm, nothing copied verbatim — author's invention.
